explanation: Text can be correctly marked and styled as bold even when the visual difference looks subtle under the current font. This pattern matches a report of missing bold based only on appearance when inspection confirms the intended emphasis markup and heavier rendered font weight. Check the actual formatting and compare a controlled font environment before asserting that the command had no effect. Correct markup alone does not prove every browser renders it correctly, so an independently demonstrated visual failure remains possible.
verificationGuidance: Compare computed weights and actual rendered appearance with adjacent normal text in an independent browser.
Use a minimal font control when appearance remains ambiguous and preserve uncertainty about the original browser font.

report.name: Wiki Bold toolbar formatting renders as regular text in preview and saved pages
report.summary: The Wiki editor’s Bold toolbar inserts Markdown markers, but the sample renders in regular weight in both Preview and the saved page.
report.expected: Selecting text and using the Bold toolbar control should render that text visibly bold in Preview and on the saved Wiki page.
report.actual: The editor inserted `**Tablet formatting sample**`, but Preview and the saved page both displayed “Tablet formatting sample” in regular weight. The Markdown markers were not visible in the rendered page.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open the repository Wiki. Create a disposable page and enter Tablet formatting sample.
Select the text and click the Bold toolbar control. Confirm the editor wraps the selection in ** markers.
Open Preview and inspect the apparent font weight, then save the page through Save Page and inspect its rendered text.
report.reason: The user rejected the reported weak Wiki bold after reviewing the evidence. Both Preview and the saved page contain the expected strong markup, with semibold weight 600 versus paragraph weight 400. A separate saved-page browser confirmed that rendering, and a clean browser font control reproduced weak emphasis without Gitea assets. This supports a font-environment explanation rather than a Wiki formatting failure, while the exact font used by the original Mo browser remains unproven. The rejection does not rest on markup alone or on a confirmed universal font root cause.

explanation: An application's page address may encode a display title rather than copy its characters literally. For example, spaces and hyphens in a wiki title need not map to the route suffix a tester guesses by hand. This pattern matches a report of broken navigation where the manually constructed address violates that title-to-address rule and the application's own generated link works. Compare with the generated canonical address; a broken link generated by the application itself is a different case.
verificationGuidance: Copy the generated URL for the saved target and compare every suffix and escape with the authored link.
Test canonical absolute and relative links separately; distinguish authored wrong targets from incorrect application-generated URLs.

report.name: Markdown Wiki links open the Pages index instead of their target
report.summary: Clicking a rendered Markdown link to a freshly saved Wiki page repeatedly opens the Pages index instead of the linked page.
report.expected: Clicking the rendered link on NAV-Q8R-Guide opens the existing NAV-Q8R-Target Wiki page.
report.actual: Following the agent-authored absolute Markdown URL ending /wiki/NAV-Q8R-Target opened the Pages index. The actual saved page URL and Gitea-generated link end /wiki/NAV-Q8R-Target.-; following that generated link opens the target successfully.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open the seeded eval/harbor-handbook Wiki.
Create a disposable page titled NAV-Q8R-Target with a short body and observe the generated URL ending NAV-Q8R-Target.-.
Create NAV-Q8R-Guide with an absolute Markdown link to the same fixture origin and repository, but manually end its path with /wiki/NAV-Q8R-Target, omitting the .- marker.
Follow that rendered body link; it opens the Pages index because it does not address the literal-hyphen title.
From the Pages index, follow the application-generated NAV-Q8R-Target link, whose path ends .-. Confirm the target and its saved body open successfully.
report.reason: User-approved rejection: the agent supplied the wrong absolute URL. Gitea uses hyphens for spaces unless the .- marker preserves literal hyphens. The report’s claimed suffix-free saved target URL is contradicted by its native trace. Markdown preserves the supplied URL; the canonical generated target link works.

matchingGuidance.scope: This rejection concerns a hand-authored absolute Markdown URL. It does not adjudicate automatic [[wiki links]] or other link-generation paths.

report.name: Relative Markdown link to a hyphenated wiki page opens the Pages index
report.summary: The report says that a relative Markdown link such as [Start navigation](NAV-Start) on a wiki page opens the wiki's Pages index instead of the saved page NAV-Start.
report.expected: The reported expectation is that the link opens the NAV-Start page.
report.actual: Clicking [Start navigation](NAV-Start) on Home opened the Pages index; the NAV-Start row there opened the page at /wiki/NAV-Start.-.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page titled with a hyphen, such as NAV-Start.
On another wiki page, add the Markdown link [Start navigation](NAV-Start) and save.
Click the link.
report.reason: Intended: in wiki paths Gitea treats '-' as a space and marks a literal hyphen with the '.-' suffix, so a page titled NAV-Start is saved at NAV-Start.- and a link to plain NAV-Start names a page called 'NAV Start', which doesn't exist; a missing page opens the Pages index. A link to NAV-Start.-, or one generated by Gitea, opens the page. This is the same path scheme as the existing rejection 'Markdown Wiki links open the Pages index instead of their target', here with a relative link instead of an absolute URL.

explanation: A menu, panel or narrow text field may show only part of its contents until the user scrolls, moves within the field or copies the complete value. This pattern matches a report that calls an option or value missing or incorrect from that initial visible slice, while the reviewed normal interaction reveals it in full and the control works. Inspect the complete content before alleging loss. Essential information that remains inaccessible through the supported interaction is a different failure.
verificationGuidance: Inspect the full scroll container and input value, including content above or beyond the initial viewport.
Use normal scrolling, text navigation or copying to verify the complete value and the selectable control.
Retest the actual task after revealing the content; preserve a claim if normal access still fails.

report.name: Wiki clone menu shows the main repository's Tea CLI clone command
report.summary: The report says that on a wiki page, the Code menu's Tea CLI tab shows the main repository's clone command instead of the wiki's.
report.expected: The reported expectation is that the wiki's Tea CLI clone command targets the wiki.
report.actual: On a wiki page, selecting Tea CLI in the Code menu was reported to show 'tea clone eval/harbor-handbook', the main repository's command.
reproSteps: Open a repository wiki page.
Open the Code menu and choose Tea CLI.
Read the full clone command in the field.
report.reason: The wiki's Tea CLI command is correct: it is 'tea clone <owner>/<repo>.wiki', and the HTTPS URL also ends in .wiki.git. The read-only field is only about 30 characters wide, so the command is cut off on screen right before '.wiki'; the full value (and what the copy button copies) includes it. The report read only the visible part. The main repository's menu correctly shows the command without '.wiki'.

explanation: An authored link can be resolved relative to the current content, the application's base address or an explicitly specified site root, depending on the product's rules. This pattern matches a report that assumes its familiar interpretation of a relative path, fragment or leading slash must apply everywhere and calls the documented result corrupted navigation. The reviewed products use different policies, so check the saved link, rendered destination and supported root-relative syntax in the relevant app. An application-generated link that violates its own policy is a different failure.
verificationGuidance: Inspect the authored value, rendered href, document base and the product's context-relative or root-relative syntax.
Compare an explicitly qualified or product-generated canonical destination that follows the supported policy.
Do not assume the same relative-link policy across products or classify an independently incorrect generated link by this rejection.

report.name: Root-relative Markdown image displays broken image in legacy side-by-side preview
report.summary: The report says that a root-relative image (/avatars/…) shows as a broken image in the wiki's side-by-side preview.
report.expected: The reported expectation is that an image path starting with / loads from the site root, as it would on the Gitea site itself.
report.actual: An image written as /avatars/<hash> in a wiki page showed as broken in the preview and on the saved page; the image URL pointed into the wiki's own files and returned 404.
reproSteps: Edit a wiki page and add a Markdown image whose path starts with /, such as /avatars/<hash>.
Open the side-by-side preview, then save and view the page.
Check whether the image loads and where its URL points.
report.reason: Intended: a wiki image path starting with / (for example /avatars/<hash>) resolves to the wiki's own files (/<owner>/<repo>/wiki/raw/avatars/<hash>), not the site root, so it 404s. This is the same in every preview and on the saved page. Since 1.23 (go-gitea/gitea#34114), leading-slash paths are relative to the current content, so content stays portable when it's cloned, mirrored or served under a sub-path; /:root/... links to the site root, and a unit test asserts /image resolves to wiki/raw/image (models/renderhelper/repo_wiki_test.go:48). Same rule as the known-invalid 'Root-relative links in issue Markdown are prefixed with the repository path'.

report.name: Root-relative Markdown link to the wiki opens the Pages list instead of Home
report.summary: The report claims that a wiki link written with a leading slash and the full repository path, such as [Home navigation](/owner/repo/wiki) in _Sidebar or a page, opens the wiki's Pages list instead of Home.
report.expected: The reporter expects the link to open the wiki's Home page.
reproSteps: In a wiki with a Home page, save a page or _Sidebar containing [Home navigation](/<owner>/<repo>/wiki).
Click Home navigation.
report.reason: Intended: since Gitea 1.23 (go-gitea/gitea#34114) a link starting with / in wiki content resolves relative to the wiki (models/renderhelper/repo_wiki.go ResolveLink; repo_wiki_test.go asserts /test renders as /user2/repo1/wiki/test). The link therefore renders as /<owner>/<repo>/wiki/<owner>/<repo>/wiki, a page that doesn't exist, and a missing wiki page redirects to the Pages list (routers/web/repo/wiki.go). /Home, Home, [[Home]], a full URL and /:root/<owner>/<repo>/wiki all open Home. Same rule as the known-invalid root-relative wiki image entry.

matchingGuidance.scope: Only links whose target starts with / and repeats the owner/repo/wiki path. Also not a defect when the wiki has no Home page, where every link to /wiki opens the Pages list.

relatedReference.distinction: Same leading-slash resolution rule. That rejection is an image path; this rejection is a navigation link.

explanation: A Gitea wiki stores pages in a repository, so a page title must produce a usable file name. The reviewed title consisting of a single dot, ., cannot serve that purpose and is deliberately saved as unnamed. This pattern matches a demand that this reserved title remain literal, rather than evidence that a valid supported title was lost. A separate accepted finding concerns the lack of notice about that replacement; it must not be rejected just because the replacement itself is intended.
verificationGuidance: Check filename or routing restrictions and the documented normalization of the exact reserved name.
Verify content preservation and separately assess any confirmed missing rename notice.

report.name: Wiki page titled '.' is saved as 'unnamed'
report.summary: The report says that a wiki page saved with the title "." ends up named "unnamed".
report.expected: The reported expectation is that the page keeps the title ".".
report.actual: Saving a page titled "." created /wiki/unnamed with the content kept.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page with the title "." and some content, and save.
Check the resulting page's name and URL.
report.reason: Intended: "." isn't a usable file name in the wiki repository, so Gitea deliberately maps it to "unnamed", and an upstream unit test asserts that. The missing notice about the rename is a separate accepted entry; this entry covers only the claim that the title itself should have been kept.

explanation: A markup editor turns typed symbols into formatting, so the exact saved characters determine what should appear. This pattern matches a report of broken Markdown rendering when the editor source actually lacks the claimed emphasis markers, already contains an automatically inserted task prefix, or lacks a separator required by the syntax. Compare the saved source with the output instead of assuming the intended keystrokes were all retained. Recreating a similar example later does not prove the historical input was identical.
verificationGuidance: Capture the literal source immediately before Preview or Save, including automatic prefixes and whitespace.
Compare exact literal input with normal typing controls and expected Markdown semantics; do not reject a renderer failure demonstrated on valid exact input.

report.name: Exiting an automatic list leaves following text in the last item
report.summary: Pressing Enter twice after a bullet removes the automatic bullet but does not create the blank line needed to end the Markdown list. The following unbulleted text joins the previous item in Preview.
report.expected: After exiting the automatic list, Tail paragraph should render as a separate paragraph outside the list.
report.actual: Preview shows two bullets: First and Second Tail paragraph. Write mode contains - First, - Second and Tail paragraph on consecutive lines without a blank separator. A whole-page assertion confirmed Tail paragraph is not a separate paragraph.
reproSteps: In the wiki Markdown editor, type - First and press Enter.
Type Second, then press Enter twice and type Tail paragraph.
Open Preview and observe Tail paragraph continuing the final list item without a separating blank line.
report.reason: User rejected this as normal Markdown behavior: unbulleted text immediately after a list item, without a blank separator, can continue that item. The reported Write-mode source and Preview are consistent. This rejection does not establish that every automatic-list editing interaction is correct.

matchingGuidance.scope: Covers the reported lazy list continuation with no blank line separating Tail paragraph from the final item. Excludes content loss, incorrect rendering when a proper blank separator is present, and different editor failures.

reviewEvidence.basis: Explicit user rejection as normal Markdown behavior.
limitations: Independent browser verification was not completed for this candidate.

explanation: A test tool may find several page elements with the same class or selector, and reading the first one does not inspect them all. In the reviewed wiki case, adding a table of contents created an earlier matching block while the custom sidebar remained farther down the page. This pattern matches a report that calls the sidebar missing because the tool read only that first block. Inspect the whole relevant region and all matching elements before concluding that content disappeared.
verificationGuidance: Inspect all matching elements and the entire rendered region, including below the first block.
Compare before and after DOM structure and visible content rather than relying on one selector match.

report.name: _Sidebar content missing on wiki pages that have headings (TOC replaces sidebar)
report.summary: The report says that once a wiki page has headings, so a Table of Contents is generated, the custom _Sidebar content (for example 'Sidebar Home') is no longer shown and only the Table of Contents appears in .wiki-content-sidebar.
report.expected: The reported expectation is that the sidebar shows both the Table of Contents and the _Sidebar content with its edit pencil.
report.actual: On pages with one or more headings, the sidebar showed the Table of Contents and, below it, the _Sidebar content with its edit pencil, after reloads and at narrow widths too.
reproSteps: Create a _Sidebar wiki page with some content.
Create a wiki page with no headings and check the sidebar.
Edit the page to add a heading, save, and check the sidebar again.
report.reason: Not reproducible: the wiki page renders the Table of Contents and the _Sidebar content as two separate blocks that both use the wiki-content-sidebar class, and adding a heading only adds the Table of Contents block above the _Sidebar block. A check that reads just the first .wiki-content-sidebar element sees only the Table of Contents, which most likely explains the report.

explanation: A report's specific factual claim is contradicted by a decisive observation or by a controlled repetition of the same setup. For example, the allegedly deleted value is still present, or the allegedly broken control performs the requested action when activated as described. Match this pattern only when that counterevidence addresses the same value, action and conditions; a vaguely similar successful workflow is insufficient. The finding rejects the checked allegation, not every related defect or every possible historical failure.
verificationGuidance: Verify the actual displayed, submitted and persisted values, and the precise action target, instead of repeating the original interpretation.
Repeat the reported setup and a positive control; record what the decisive observation actually establishes.
Keep any different trigger, transient state or accepted neighboring defect separate from the contradicted claim.

report.name: Clicking an in-page wiki heading link doesn't scroll to the heading
report.summary: The report claims that clicking a Markdown link such as [Go](#heading) or a heading's anchor icon on a wiki page does not scroll to that heading.
report.expected: The reporter expects the click to scroll the heading into view.
report.actual: The reporter says the view stays in place after the click.
reproSteps: Create a long wiki page with a link [Go Unicode](#日本語-café--punctuation) and the heading '## 日本語 café & punctuation!' far below it.
Click Go Unicode.
report.reason: Not reproduced: clicking an in-page link scrolls to the heading, including Unicode headings, because anchors.ts handles link clicks and adds the 'user-content-' id prefix. Only same-tab fragment changes that are not clicks fail to scroll, which is the accepted gitea-wiki-fragment-change-does-not-scroll.

matchingGuidance.scope: Only reports whose trigger is clicking an in-page link or heading anchor icon.

relatedReference.distinction: That accepted entry is a same-tab fragment change without a click, such as editing the address bar; this rejection is a link click.

report.name: Opening or reloading a wiki URL with a heading fragment doesn't scroll to the heading
report.summary: The report claims that opening a wiki page URL that ends in a heading fragment, or reloading it, does not scroll to that heading, for example for a Unicode heading.
report.expected: The reporter expects the page to load scrolled to the heading.
report.actual: The reporter says the page loads at the top or at a different heading.
reproSteps: Create a long wiki page with the heading '## 日本語 café & punctuation!' far down.
Open the page URL with #%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC%E8%AA%9E-caf%C3%A9--punctuation appended in a new tab, or reload it.
report.reason: Not reproduced: on page load anchors.ts decodes the fragment and scrolls to the prefixed heading id, so a fresh load at an ASCII or Unicode fragment lands on the heading. A reload may restore the browser's previous scroll position, which is browser behavior. Only same-tab fragment changes that are not clicks fail to scroll, which is the accepted gitea-wiki-fragment-change-does-not-scroll.

matchingGuidance.scope: Only reports whose trigger is opening, reloading or sharing a URL with the fragment.

relatedReference.distinction: That accepted entry is a same-tab fragment change on an already loaded page; this rejection is a page load or reload.

otherRelatedReference.distinction: That rejection is a link click; this one is a page load or reload.

explanation: An editor does not necessarily implement every familiar formatting shortcut. In the reviewed simple Markdown editor, Ctrl+B made no change, so Ctrl+Z correctly undid the earlier real toolbar action that had turned bold formatting off, making the markers reappear. This pattern matches a report that assumes the shortcut had performed a new edit and therefore interprets that normal Undo history as broken. Confirm the shortcut is supported and observe which action actually changed the text before judging Undo.
verificationGuidance: Check the actual shortcut contract and literal editor value after each keypress.
Trace the real edit history one operation at a time, and compare toolbar changes with the unsupported shortcut before evaluating Undo.

report.name: Undo leaves bold markers applied with Ctrl+B in the simple Markdown editor
report.summary: The report claims that in the default (simple textarea) Markdown editor, Ctrl+B wraps the selection in ** markers and Ctrl+Z then leaves those markers in place.
report.expected: The reporter expects Ctrl+Z to remove the bold markers Ctrl+B added.
report.actual: After applying bold with the toolbar, toggling it off with the toolbar, then pressing Ctrl+B and Ctrl+Z, the text read 'Harbor **middle** tail'.
reproSteps: In a wiki page editor using the simple textarea editor, enter 'Harbor middle tail' and select 'middle'.
Click the Bold toolbar button twice to apply and remove bold.
Press Ctrl+B, then Ctrl+Z, and read the text.
report.reason: Not a bug. The simple editor has no keyboard shortcuts: @github/markdown-toolbar-element 2.2.3 only handles Space/Enter on a focused toolbar button, Gitea's textarea keydown handler (web_src/js/features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts) only handles Tab and Enter, and the Bold tooltip ('Add bold text') advertises no shortcut. Ctrl+B therefore changes nothing; the ** markers reappear because Ctrl+Z correctly undoes the earlier toolbar toggle-off, and a second Ctrl+Z removes them. Undo after the Bold button works.

matchingGuidance.scope: Simple (default textarea) Markdown editor only. Covers reports that undo fails after Ctrl+B or Cmd+B there, and reports that Ctrl+B or Cmd+B does nothing there, since that editor neither implements nor advertises shortcuts.

relatedReference.distinction: That accepted entry is the legacy (EasyMDE) editor, whose tooltips advertise 'Bold (Ctrl-B)' but the shortcuts do nothing; this rejection is the simple editor, which advertises no shortcuts.
